claims: The cone uses the fixed original source and its actual earliest chain entries. Original target reachability gives cone nesting.
Every chain visited by a valid original-source path belongs to its target cone, using actual entry membership and legal shortcut reachability.
A nonprefix chain entry occurs in the suffix; reachability from the pivot to that entry makes membership in an inaccessible guard cone impossible.
The disjoint union of the guard cone and all original nonprefix chains embeds into the old target cone. Exact cardinal subtraction gives the exported additive depletion inequality.
scope: No recomputation of entries with a rebased source.
No general cubic progress or runtime theorem.
